paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧סֶף אַבְרָהָ֛ם וַיִּקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה וּשְׁמָ֥הּ קְטוּרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Avraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah.

notes.official:
**Vv 1-4 narrate Avraham's third domestic configuration: Keturah and her six sons, and the seven grandsons through Yokshan and Midyan.** The Keturah-line is one of the HB's three collateral-Avrahamic-genealogies — paired with the Yishma'elite twelve (vv 12-18) and the Nahor twelve (Gen 22:20-24) — and assigns each to a tribal-political register peripheral to but related to the covenantal Yitzchaq-line.

The Keturah-line's tribal-onomastic content overlaps substantially with North-Arabian and Trans-Jordanian peoples attested elsewhere in the HB and in the ANE record. **Midyan** is the eponym of the Midianites — the wilderness-confederation attested at Exod 2:15-21 (Moses' Midianite father-in-law Jethro / Reuel), Num 22-24 (the Balaam-narrative), Num 25 (the Baal-Peor incident), and Judg 6-8 (the Gideon cycle); **Knauf** 1988 *Midian* and **Mendenhall** 1992 reconstruct the historical Midianite-confederation as an Iron-Age North-Arabian camel-pastoralist league. **Sheva** and **Dedan** recur at Gen 10:7 (via Cush — a different genealogical lineage, suggesting the names attach to peoples rather than to single ancestors), Isa 21:13 (the Dedanite caravans), Jer 25:23, Ezek 25:13 and 27:15 (Dedan in the Tyre lament), Ezek 38:13 (Sheva and Dedan among the Gog opponents); the toponyms map onto historical North-Arabian oasis-confederations attested in the Neo-Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian record. **Ephah** is attested in Isa 60:6 (with Midyan, in the caravan-imagery) and in the Tiglath-Pileser III annals (Ḫa-a-a-pa-a in the 8th-century North-Arabian campaign records). **Knauf** 1988 treats the Keturah-line as preserving real Late-Iron-Age North-Arabian tribal data, not ad hoc fiction.

The Keturah-narrative's editorial-function. The Keturah-genealogy at vv 1-4, paired with the inheritance-distribution at vv 5-6 (Yitzchaq receives *all that he had*; the concubine-sons receive *gifts* and are sent away *eastward, to the east country*), structurally **closes the Avrahamic peripheral-line** before the chapter pivots to the central Yitzchaq-line at v 19. The vv 5-6 inheritance-distribution functions in the same juridical register as the Gen 21:8-21 expulsion of Hagar and Yishma'el: the central covenantal line is reserved for Yitzchaq; the peripheral lines receive blessing-but-not-covenant.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 173-174; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 396-397; Knauf 1988 *Midian*; Mendenhall 1992 *ABD* IV: 'Midian'.

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֣לֶד ל֗וֹ אֶת־זִמְרָן֙ וְאֶת־יָקְשָׁ֔ן וְאֶת־מְדָ֖ן וְאֶת־מִדְיָ֑ן וְאֶת־יִשְׁבָּ֖ק וְאֶת־שֽׁוּחַ׃

i18n.en: And she bore him Zimran, and Yokshan, and Medan, and Midyan, and Yishbak, and Shuach.

paragraphs.text: וְיָקְשָׁ֣ן יָלַ֔ד אֶת־שְׁבָ֖א וְאֶת־דְּדָ֑ן וּבְנֵ֣י דְדָ֔ן הָי֛וּ אַשּׁוּרִ֥ם וּלְטוּשִׁ֖ים וּלְאֻמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And Yokshan begot Sheva and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Ashurim and Letushim and Le'ummim.

paragraphs.text: וּבְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֗ן עֵיפָ֤ה וָעֵ֙פֶר֙ וַחֲנֹ֔ךְ וַאֲבִידָ֖ע וְאֶלְדָּעָ֑ה כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י קְטוּרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Midyan: Ephah, and Epher, and Chanokh, and Avida, and Elda'ah. All these were the sons of Keturah.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ לְיִצְחָֽק׃

i18n.en: And Avraham gave all that he had to Yitzchaq.

paragraphs.text: וְלִבְנֵ֤י הַפִּֽילַגְשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם נָתַ֥ן אַבְרָהָ֖ם מַתָּנֹ֑ת וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֞ם מֵעַ֨ל יִצְחָ֤ק בְּנוֹ֙ בְּעוֹדֶ֣נּוּ חַ֔י קֵ֖דְמָה אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ קֶֽדֶם׃

i18n.en: But to the sons of the concubines that Avraham had, Avraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from Yitzchaq his son, while he yet lived, eastward, to the east country.

notes.official:
**Vv 5-6 stage the inheritance-distribution: Yitzchaq receives *kol-asher lo* (*all that he had*); the *bnei ha-pilagshim* (sons of the concubines) receive *mattanot* (gifts) and are sent *qedmah el-eretz qedem* (eastward to the east country).** The juridical pattern is identical to the Gen 21:8-21 expulsion of Hagar and Yishma'el: the covenantal line passes intact to the chosen son; the peripheral sons receive a partial-share and are geographically relocated outside the covenantal land.

The eastward-relocation is structurally significant. The *eretz qedem* (east country) is the HB's tropic of foreign-or-peripheral residence — Cain at Gen 4:16 *vayyeshev b-eretz Nod qidmat-Eden* (the land of Nod east of Eden); the Babel migrants at Gen 11:2 *b-nasam mi-qedem* (in their journey from the east); Lot's descendants at Gen 19:30-38 (the Ammonites and Moabites east of the Dead Sea); the Yishma'elites at Gen 25:18 (*from Chavilah to Shur ... toward Ashur*). The covenant-line dwells in the central land; the peripheral lines settle east. The pattern is editorially-deliberate.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 173-174; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 397-398.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה יְמֵ֛י שְׁנֵֽי־חַיֵּ֥י אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־חָ֑י מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְחָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Avraham expired, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years, and was gathered to his people.

notes.official:
**The patriarchal-good-death formula.** The chapter's death-notice for Avraham — *va-yamot Avraham b-seyvah tovah, zaqen v-savea, va-ye'asef el-amav* (*and Avraham died in a good old age, an old man and satisfied, and was gathered to his people*) — deploys the HB's canonical *zaqen u-s'va yamim* formula in its short-form variant *zaqen v-savea* (*old and satisfied*, without the explicit *yamim* / *days*). The lexical-family is treated in the `zaqen-u-s-va-yamim` glossary entry, which lists Gen 25:8 in its appliesTo (set at v2.8.0) and treats the variant as part of the formula's reach.

The formula's structural function is to mark the figure as recipient of completed divine favor — the patriarchal mode of departure, death at the natural end of a long full life, in contrast to violent or premature death. Cross-corpus: Avraham (here), Yitzchaq (Gen 35:29), David (1 Chr 29:28), Jehoiada the priest (2 Chr 24:15), Job (42:17). The Avraham-instance is the canonical-first occurrence in the patriarchal narratives.

Two additional editorial-notes. The verb *va-ye'asef el-amav* (*and was gathered to his people*) is the canonical HB death-formula for **familial-ancestral reunion** — Avraham is gathered to his pre-Israelite ancestors (his father Terach died in Haran at Gen 11:32, but the broader *amav* includes the pre-Sumerian patriarchal-line). The formula is repeated for Yishma'el at v 17 — a structural pairing-by-formula that emphasizes the Avrahamic-paternity of both sons. The implicit pre-Sheol theology of the *gathered-to-his-people* formula is a pre-eschatological-conception of post-mortem familial-clan-reunion, not the developed Sheol-or-resurrection theology of later HB literature.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 174; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 398; Alter *Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 128.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְבְּר֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ יִצְחָ֤ק וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ בָּנָ֔יו אֶל־מְעָרַ֖ת הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֑ה אֶל־שְׂדֵ֞ה עֶפְרֹ֤ן בֶּן־צֹ֙חַר֙ הַֽחִתִּ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq and Yishma'el his sons buried him in the cave of Makhpelah, in the field of Efron the son of Tzochar the Chitti, which is before Mamre,

notes.official:
**Yitzchaq and Yishma'el bury Avraham together at Makhpelah — the only HB scene of the two brothers acting in concert after the Gen 21 expulsion.** The reunion-at-burial is editorially-deliberate and is the structural-completion of the Avraham-cycle. The pre-expulsion Gen 16 conception of Yishma'el and the post-expulsion Gen 21 separation are resolved at the patriarchal-burial: the two sons stand together at the cave of Makhpelah where Sarah herself was buried (Gen 23:19), and where Avraham now joins her.

The naming-order *Yitzchaq v-Yishma'el banav* (*Yitzchaq and Yishma'el his sons*) places Yitzchaq first — chronologically the younger son but the covenantal-firstborn. The order is editorial: the covenantal-firstborn-priority is preserved in the burial-order, but the joint-action is preserved in the conjunction.

The reception traditions extend the reunion: **Genesis Rabbah 38:12** reads the reunion as Yishma'el's *teshuvah* (repentance) — Yishma'el yields precedence to Yitzchaq at the burial as an act of acknowledgment of the covenantal hierarchy; **Pirqei de-Rabbi Eliezer 30** similarly reads the reunion as a reconciliation-moment. The reunion-at-burial pattern recurs structurally at Gen 35:29 (Esav and Ya'aqov burying Yitzchaq together) and at Gen 50:13 (the twelve sons burying Ya'aqov), forming a HB-internal sub-theme of fraternal-reunion-at-patriarchal-burial.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 173; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 397-398; Genesis Rabbah 38:12; Pirqei de-Rabbi Eliezer 30.

paragraphs.text: הַשָּׂדֶ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־קָנָ֥ה אַבְרָהָ֖ם מֵאֵ֣ת בְּנֵי־חֵ֑ת שָׁ֛מָּה קֻבַּ֥ר אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְשָׂרָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: the field which Avraham purchased from the sons of Chet. There was Avraham buried, and Sarah his wife.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת אַבְרָהָ֔ם וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יִצְחָ֔ק עִם־בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִֽי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And it came to pass after the death of Avraham, that the Elohim blessed Yitzchaq his son. And Yitzchaq dwelt by Be'er Lachai Ro'i.

notes.official:
**The verse closes the Avraham-cycle with the Elohim's blessing of Yitzchaq and Yitzchaq's settlement at Be'er Lachai Ro'i.** The well-name is treated in the `beer-lachai-roi` glossary entry, which lists Gen 25:11 in its appliesTo (set at v2.13.0). The recurrence of the well at 25:11 is editorially-deliberate: Yitzchaq inherits not only the seed-promise but the residence-site of Hagar's foundational divine-encounter at Gen 16:13-14. The well of the *El Ro'i* (the God who sees Hagar) becomes Yitzchaq's dwelling-place after his father's death — a structural-thematic coupling of the Hagar-narrative and the Yitzchaq-narrative that the editor leaves implicit rather than commenting on.

The construction *va-yeshev Yitzchaq im Be'er Lachai Ro'i* uses the preposition *im* (*with, alongside*) rather than the more common *b-* (*at, in*) for residence-locale. The *im*-construction is unusual: residences are typically located *at* / *in* a place, not *with* a place. The unusual idiom is sometimes read (Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 174) as suggesting a more-than-locational relationship — Yitzchaq dwells *in association with* the well, treating the cultic-site as a fixed-point of his residence-pattern rather than as a transit-feature. The reading is plausible but not lexically-required.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 174; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 398.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תֹּלְדֹ֥ת יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֜ה הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית שִׁפְחַ֥ת שָׂרָ֖ה לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃

i18n.en: Now these are the generations of Yishma'el, Avraham's son, whom Hagar the Mitsri'it, Sarah's handmaid, bore to Avraham.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל בִּשְׁמֹתָ֖ם לְתוֹלְדֹתָ֑ם בְּכֹ֤ר יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ נְבָיֹ֔ת וְקֵדָ֥ר וְאַדְבְּאֵ֖ל וּמִבְשָֽׂם׃

i18n.en: And these are the names of the sons of Yishma'el, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Yishma'el, Nevayot; and Qedar, and Adbe'el, and Mivsam,

paragraphs.text: וּמִשְׁמָ֥ע וְדוּמָ֖ה וּמַשָּֽׂא׃

i18n.en: and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,

paragraphs.text: חֲדַ֣ד וְתֵימָ֔א יְט֥וּר נָפִ֖ישׁ וָקֵֽדְמָה׃

i18n.en: Hadad, and Tema, Yetur, Nafish, and Qedmah.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֞ם בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמֹתָ֔ם בְּחַצְרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְטִֽירֹתָ֑ם שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר נְשִׂיאִ֖ם לְאֻמֹּתָֽם׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Yishma'el, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments; twelve princes according to their nations.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וַיִּגְוַ֣ע וַיָּ֔מָת וַיֵּאָ֖סֶף אֶל־עַמָּֽיו׃

i18n.en: And these are the years of the life of Yishma'el, a hundred and thirty-seven years; and he expired, and died, and was gathered to his people.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁכְּנ֨וּ מֵֽחֲוִילָ֜ה עַד־שׁ֗וּר אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י מִצְרַ֔יִם בֹּאֲכָ֖ה אַשּׁ֑וּרָה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י כָל־אֶחָ֖יו נָפָֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And they dwelt from Chavilah to Shur, which is before Mitsrayim, as you go toward Ashur. He settled over against all his brethren.

notes.official:
**The verse closes the Yishma'elite-toledot by recalling the verb-frame of the Gen 16:12 *pere adam* prophecy.** The two verses use a parallel idiom — *al-pnei kol echav* (*over against all his brothers*) — with different verbs: *yishkon* (*shall dwell*) at Gen 16:12; *nafal* (*fell / settled / encamped*) at Gen 25:18. The cross-reference is editorially-deliberate and forms a Yishma'elite-narrative inclusio: the verb-frame of the naming-prophecy is recalled at the closing-formula of the Yishma'elite-genealogy. The `pere-adam-wild-ass-prophecy` glossary entry (set at v2.13.0) lists both Gen 16:12 and Gen 25:18 in its appliesTo and treats the parallel as the foundational geographical-cultic placement of the Yishma'elite confederation east-and-south of the patriarchal-Israelite land.

The verb *nafal* (qal pf 3ms — *fell / settled / encamped*) is grammatically ambiguous: (a) ASV/KJV *settled / fell* (the ambiguity preserved); (b) NJPS *settled* (neutral residence-sense, parallel to Gen 16:12 *yishkon*); (c) some critical readings *fell-apart-from* or *fell-as-by-the-sword* (the standard *fall* register; the negative-encamping sense at Jer 7:20, Judg 7:12). The ASV's *settled over against* preserves the ambiguity. **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 175-176 reads the verb neutrally as *settled*; **Alter** *Five Books of Moses* 2004 pp. 128-129 reads the verb as *encamped* with the negative-encamping overtone; **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 399 reads the verse as paralleling Gen 16:12 with verb-variation. The translation preserves the ASV-baseline ambiguity.

The geographical placement — *me-Chavilah ad-Shur asher al-pnei Mitsrayim bo'akhah Ashurah* — locates the Yishma'elites along an arc from Chavilah (probably in the eastern Arabian peninsula) through Shur (in the northern Sinai) toward Ashur (the Neo-Assyrian-period geographical-pole). The placement matches the historical North-Arabian tribal-confederation reconstructed by Knauf 1989 *Ismael*; the Tiglath-Pileser III and Ashurbanipal annals attest the Yishma'elite confederation across precisely this arc in the 8th-7th centuries BCE.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 175-176; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 399; Knauf 1989 *Ismael*; Eph'al 1982 *The Ancient Arabs*.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תּוֹלְדֹ֥ת יִצְחָ֖ק בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֑ם אַבְרָהָ֖ם הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־יִצְחָֽק׃

i18n.en: And these are the generations of Yitzchaq, Avraham's son: Avraham begot Yitzchaq.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י יִצְחָק֙ בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּקַחְתּ֣וֹ אֶת־רִבְקָ֗ה בַּת־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י מִפַּדַּ֖ן אֲרָ֑ם אֲח֛וֹת לָבָ֥ן הָאֲרַמִּ֖י ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq was forty years old when he took Rivkah, the daughter of Bethuel the Arammi of Paddan-Aram, the sister of Lavan the Arammi, to be his wife.

paragraphs.text: וַיֶּעְתַּ֨ר יִצְחָ֤ק לַֽיהוָה֙ לְנֹ֣כַח אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה הִ֑וא וַיֵּעָ֤תֶר לוֹ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַתַּ֖הַר רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq entreated YHWH for his wife, because she was barren; and YHWH was entreated of him, and Rivkah his wife conceived.

notes.official:
**The *atar*-intercession formula.** The verse stages a stylistically-deliberate qal-niphal symmetry on the prayer-root *atar* (עָתַר): Yitzchaq *va-ye'tar* (qal — *entreated*) YHWH, and YHWH *va-ye'ater* (niphal — *was entreated, allowed himself to be entreated*) him. The qal-and-niphal pairing on the same root in adjacent clauses is a HB stylistic marker for the prayer-and-answer pattern: petition uttered, petition received. The lexeme and its cross-corpus reach are treated in the `atar-l-yhwh-intercession` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).

Three editorial-notes. **(i)** Gen 25:21 is the first HB occurrence of the *atar* prayer-root. The lexeme is distinct from the broader HB prayer-vocabulary — *hithpallel* (the formal-petition root, see the existing `hithpallel-first-prayer-occurrence` entry at Gen 20:7,17), *darash* (the oracle-consultation root, see the companion `darash-yhwh-seeking-oracle` entry, Gen 25:22 immediately following), *qara b-shem YHWH* (the cultic-invocation formula). The *atar* register is specifically intercessory: petition offered for someone else, often in afflictive-context. The Yitzchaq-Rivkah barrenness-petition is the canonical-first instance and seeds the lexeme's later reach into the Mosaic plague-intercessions (Exod 8-10), Manoah's barrenness-petition for the future Samson (Judg 13:8 — a deliberate structural parallel to the Gen 25 scene), and the Manasseh-repentance (2 Chr 33:13,19).

**(ii)** The *l-nokhach ishto* clause (לְנֹכַח אִשְׁתּוֹ) is grammatically ambiguous. *L-nokhach* (from *nokhach* — *over against, opposite, facing*) can be read either (a) **prepositionally** (*on behalf of / for his wife*, the standard intercessory-direction; ASV/KJV/NRSV read this way) or (b) **spatially** (*facing his wife*, suggesting Yitzchaq prayed in Rivkah's physical presence; Alter 2004 reads this way). Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 179 prefers the spatial-presence sense: the petition is offered in shared-physical-presence, the patriarchal-intercession not a private act but a conjugal-shared petition. The translation preserves the ASV *for his wife* with the spatial-presence reading flagged in apparatus.

**(iii)** The Yitzchaq-Rivkah barrenness-pattern recapitulates the Sarah-Avraham barrenness-pattern of Gen 11:30-21:7 and prefigures the Rachel-Ya'aqov barrenness-pattern of Gen 29:31-30:24. The three-generation matriarchal-barrenness sequence is structurally deliberate. The chronological-detail at vv 20 and 26 (Yitzchaq at forty at marriage; Yitzchaq at sixty at the twins' birth) frames the *atar*-prayer as a twenty-year intercession.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 178-179; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 413-414; Greenberg *Biblical Prose Prayer* 1983 pp. 7-8, 19-21; Wagner *Beten und Klagen* 1971.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתְרֹֽצֲצ֤וּ הַבָּנִים֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔הּ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אִם־כֵּ֔ן לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה אָנֹ֑כִי וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ לִדְרֹ֥שׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why do I live? And she went to inquire of YHWH.

notes.official:
**The first HB occurrence of *darash YHWH*.** Rivkah, distressed by the intrauterine struggle of the twins, *va-telekh li-drosh et-YHWH* — *and she went to inquire of YHWH*. The verse is the lexical-foundational instance of the HB's oracle-consultation lexeme, the verb-and-construction that names the act of seeking divine guidance through an authorized channel (priest, prophet, oracle-site). The lexeme and its cross-corpus reach are treated in the `darash-yhwh-seeking-oracle` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).

The *darash YHWH* lexical-tradition is corpus-spanning. Principal occurrences after Gen 25:22: Exod 18:15 (Moses' Mosaic-judicial-oracle role); **1 Sam 9:9** (the canonical lexical-historical note on the *ro'eh*/*navi* shift — *for he who is now called a Prophet was formerly called a Seer when a man went to inquire of God*); 1 Sam 28:6-7 (Saul before Endor, the Yahwistic-frustrated-and-medium-substituted scene); 1 Kgs 14:5 (the Ahijah-Jeroboam oracle); 1 Kgs 22:5-8 (the Jehoshaphat-Ahab Ramoth-Gilead inquiry and the Micaiah-court-prophet tension); 2 Kgs 1:2-16 (the Ahaziah-Baal-Zebub scene with Elijah's three-fold rebuke on consultation-channel-legitimacy); 2 Kgs 22:13-18 (Josiah's reform Huldah-consultation, the second-named-female-prophetic-consultation of the HB and the structural-parallel to Rivkah here); Jer 21:2, 37:7 (the Zedekiah-Jeremiah inquiries); Ezek 14:1-11, 20:1-3 (the elders-of-Israel inquiries during exile).

**Where did Rivkah go to inquire?** The MT is editorially-silent. The interpretive-distribution: **(a) the rabbinic-canonical reading** (Targum Pseudo-Jonathan, Genesis Rabbah 63:6, Rashi) locates the consultation at the *yeshivah* of Shem (the patriarchal-pre-Levitical prophetic-channel in the rabbinic chronology); **(b) the patriarchal-altar-site reading** (Ibn Ezra, some modern conservative commentators) locates the consultation at one of the named altar-sites — Be'er Lachai Ro'i (v 11), Hebron / Mamre, or Beer-Sheva; **(c) the modern critical reading** (Sarna, Westermann) preserves the silence as deliberate — the patriarchal-period does not yet have an institutional consultation-channel; **(d) the direct-divine-encounter reading** takes v 23's *va-yomer YHWH lah* (*and YHWH said to her*) as the unmediated divine response. The textual silence is the editorial-point and the translation preserves it.

**NT reception at Rom 9:10-13** reads the v 23 oracle (the divine response to Rivkah's *darash*) as the paradigm of divine election prior to action. The reception belongs to the v 23 commentary (see the `rav-yaavod-tzair-younger-displaces-elder` entry); the v 22 *darash* is the petition-act preceding the oracle.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 180; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 415; Wagner *Beten und Klagen* 1971; Greenberg *Biblical Prose Prayer* 1983; Genesis Rabbah 63:6; Rashi at Gen 25:22.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה לָ֗הּ שְׁנֵ֤י גיים [גוֹיִם֙] בְּבִטְנֵ֔ךְ וּשְׁנֵ֣י לְאֻמִּ֔ים מִמֵּעַ֖יִךְ יִפָּרֵ֑דוּ וּלְאֹם֙ מִלְאֹ֣ם יֶֽאֱמָ֔ץ וְרַ֖ב יַעֲבֹ֥ד צָעִֽיר׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to her, Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

notes.official:
**The chapter's oracular keystone — and one of the HB's most theologically-load-bearing verses.** *Shnei goyim b-vitnekh u-shnei l'umim mi-me'ayikh yipparedu, u-l-om mi-l-om ye'ematz, v-rav ya'avod tza'ir* — *Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your bowels; the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger*. Three distinct issues at the verse, each treated in detail in the `rav-yaavod-tzair-younger-displaces-elder` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).

**(a) The ketiv/qere on *goyim*.** The MT ketiv reads גיים (defective plural, ambiguous pointing); the qere reads גוֹיִם (full *goyim*). The qere is standard ASV/KJV/NRSV/NJPS practice and the translation follows it. The defective ketiv has generated multiple interpretive proposals — scribal-lapse, paronomasia with *ge'im* (proud-ones), the rabbinic *b. Avodah Zarah 11a* reading of the ketiv as hint at the proud-empires Rome and Persia.

**(b) Subject-ambiguity at *v-rav ya'avod tza'ir*.** The Hebrew word-order leaves the subject grammatically ambiguous. **Reading 1 (dominant: ASV/KJV/NRSV/NJPS, LXX, rabbinic-canonical):** *the elder shall serve the younger* (*rav* = subject, *tza'ir* = object). **Reading 2 (minority: Speiser AB 1964; NJPS footnote):** *the elder, the younger shall serve* (*rav* = object, *tza'ir* = subject). The translation follows R1 — supported by Hebrew word-order convention, the narrative outcome of Gen 25-36 (Esav loses the birthright; Ya'aqov receives both birthright and blessing), the LXX's unambiguous *ho meizōn douleusei tō elassoni*, and the rabbinic-canonical tradition. **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 181 documents both readings and presents R1 as dominant; **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 415 acknowledges the ambiguity as 'a real possibility in the Hebrew' but reads R1 as supported by the narrative outcome.

**(c) Pauline reception at Rom 9:10-13.** Paul cites the verse (LXX: *ho meizōn douleusei tō elassoni*) at Romans 9:12 as the proof-text for divine election prior to action: *for the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand*. The reception is foundational for two distinct interpretive traditions: **(i) the Calvinist / Reformed** reading takes the verse as evidence of double-predestination at the individual soteriological level (Calvin *Institutes* III.21-24; Westminster Confession III; canons of Dort); **(ii) the Arminian / Wesleyan / modern Catholic** reading reads the verse as election-of-corporate-peoples — the *meizōn / elassoni* naming the corporate destinies of Edom and Israel as nations rather than the individual-soteriological status of Esav and Ya'aqov as persons. Modern critical NT scholarship (Cranfield ICC, Dunn WBC, Käsemann) broadly sides with the corporate-peoples reading. **The Pauline reception is flagged-not-preempted.** The Gen 25:23 verse itself is editorially-confined to the patriarchal-political register (the *two nations* / *two peoples* opening clauses); the NT-reception belongs downstream and is documented in apparatus but not adjudicated here.

**The younger-displaces-elder pattern.** Gen 25:23 is the foundational HB instance of the *younger-displaces-elder* narrative pattern that recurs structurally across the Genesis arc: Abel over Cain (Gen 4); Yitzchaq over Yishma'el (Gen 17, 21); Ya'aqov over Esav (Gen 25-28, here); Yosef over the elder brothers (Gen 37, 41-50); Ephraim over Manasseh (Gen 48); Perez over Zerach (Gen 38:27-30, structurally restaging this verse's twin-birth). The pattern is editorially-coordinated and asserts the principle of *election over primogeniture* — divine selection operating by criteria other than birth-order. The HB extends the pattern into the post-Genesis material: Moses over Aaron, David over his elder brothers, Solomon over Adonijah.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 178-181; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 414-416; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 176-177; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 195-196; Cranfield *Romans 9-16* ICC 1979; Dunn *Romans 9-16* WBC 1988; Käsemann *Commentary on Romans* 1980; Genesis Rabbah 63:7.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְלְא֥וּ יָמֶ֖יהָ לָלֶ֑דֶת וְהִנֵּ֥ה תוֹמִ֖ם בְּבִטְנָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֤א הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ אַדְמוֹנִ֔י כֻּלּ֖וֹ כְּאַדֶּ֣רֶת שֵׂעָ֑ר וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ שְׁמ֖וֹ עֵשָֽׂו׃

i18n.en: And the first came forth ruddy, all over like a hairy mantle; and they called his name Esav.

notes.official:
**The elder twin's birth-description loads two paronomastic name-plays onto Esav.** *Va-yetze ha-rishon admoni, kulo k-aderet sear, va-yiqr'u shemo Esav* — *and the first came forth ruddy, all over like a hairy mantle; and they called his name Esav*. Two name-plays are seeded at the birth and realized programmatically later:

**(a) *admoni* (ruddy) → *Edom* (Red).** The reddish coloration is paronomastically linked to *adom* (*red*), which becomes the explicit etymology of Esav's secondary-name *Edom* at v 30 (*therefore was his name called Edom*). The two-stage name-play — *admoni* at birth, *adom* at the lentil-stew — structurally brackets the Esav-naming-arc across vv 25-30.

**(b) *sear* (hair) → *Seir* (the Edomite mountain-range).** The hairy-mantle imagery is paronomastically linked to *Seir* (the proper-noun toponym of the Edomite mountains, identified with Esav's territory at Gen 32:4, 33:14-16, 36:8-9, Deut 2:4-5). The link is not made explicit at v 25 but is seeded for the later Esav-Edom-Seir compound-identity.

The name *Esav* itself is etymologically opaque — BDB derives it from an unattested root *asah*; HALOT marks it 'origin uncertain'. The v 25 narrative loads paronomastic foreshadows onto Esav's birth (*admoni* for Edom; *sear* for Seir) without grounding the name *Esav* itself. The editorial-effect is a multiple-name-etymology compression in which the elder twin's *secondary* names carry the paronomastic-etymological work. The cluster is treated in the `esau-edom-name-etymology-double-play` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 181; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 416; Knauf 1988 *Midian*; Bartlett *Edom and the Edomites* 1989.

paragraphs.text: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֞ן יָצָ֣א אָחִ֗יו וְיָד֤וֹ אֹחֶ֙זֶת֙ בַּעֲקֵ֣ב עֵשָׂ֔ו וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיִצְחָ֛ק בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה בְּלֶ֥דֶת אֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And after that came forth his brother, and his hand had hold on Esav's heel; and his name was called Ya'aqov. And Yitzchaq was sixty years old when she bore them.

notes.official:
**The first explicit Ya'aqov-name-etymology.** *V-acharei-ken yatza achiv v-yado ochezet ba-aqev Esav va-yiqra shemo Ya'aqov* — *and after that came forth his brother, and his hand had hold on Esav's heel, and his name was called Ya'aqov*. The name *Ya'aqov* (יַעֲקֹב) is paronomastically linked to *aqev* (עָקֵב — *heel*) via the shared consonantal root *ʿ-q-b*: Ya'aqov is the *heel-grasper*, named at the moment of birth from the gesture of grasping his elder twin's heel.

The name's double-etymology — *heel* (the body-part at birth) and *supplant* (the denominative verb-action realized in subsequent narrative) — is editorially-load-bearing across the entire Ya'aqov-arc. The supplant-sense is *not* activated at v 26 (the verse uses only the neutral *heel*-imagery) but is **HB-internal-explicitly** derived at two later verses: **Gen 27:36** — Esav's lament after the blessing-deception, *ha-khi qara shmo Ya'aqov va-ya'aqveni zeh paamayim* — *is it not rightly that his name is called Ya'aqov, for he has supplanted me these two times*; **Hos 12:4** — *ba-beten aqav et-achiv* — *in the womb he supplanted his brother*. The lexical-family and the supplant-trajectory are treated in the `yaakov-name-etymology-aqev-supplant` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).

**The full Ya'aqov-arc is structurally framed by the *aqev* / *aqav* etymological-trajectory**: from heel-grasp (here at birth) through serial-supplant-acts (the birthright-sale at vv 29-34, the blessing-deception at ch 27, the Lavan-flocks departure at ch 31) to the wrestling-rename at Penuel (Gen 32:25-33), where Ya'aqov is renamed *Yisra'el* (*one who strives with El*) and is left limping — the heel-injury inverts the heel-grasping birth-gesture, the supplanter is himself wounded in the *kaf yerekh* (socket-of-the-thigh) and walks with a limp thereafter.

**Historical-onomastic context.** The name *Ya'aqov* (or *Ya'aqov-el*) is attested in 2nd-millennium-BCE Egyptian and Akkadian sources outside the Hebrew Bible: the Hyksos king *Ya'qub-har* / *Ya'qub-her* (17th century BCE, preserved on scarabs and seals), the Thutmose III topographical lists at Karnak (15th century BCE; *y-ʿ-q-b-ʾ-r*, likely *Ya'aqov-El*), and Old Babylonian / Mari cuneiform attestations of *Ia-aḫ-qu-ub-el* and variants. The HB Ya'aqov-narrative is grounded in a real West-Semitic name-stock; the etymology (heel / supplant) is the HB-internal narrative-theological interpretation of an existing name.

**Chronological note.** The verse closes with *v-Yitzchaq ben shishim shanah b-ledet otam* — *and Yitzchaq was sixty years old when she bore them*. The detail frames the twin-birth as twenty years after Yitzchaq's marriage to Rivkah (Gen 25:20: forty at marriage), staging the *atar*-prayer of v 21 as a twenty-year intercession.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 181-182; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 416-417; Albright 1941 *BASOR* 81; Mendenhall 1958 *BASOR* 152; Hosea 12:4 commentary in Wolff *Hosea* Hermeneia 1974.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּגְדְּלוּ֙ הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וַיְהִ֣י עֵשָׂ֗ו אִ֛ישׁ יֹדֵ֥עַ צַ֖יִד אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֶ֑ה וְיַעֲקֹב֙ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֔ם יֹשֵׁ֖ב אֹהָלִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the boys grew; and Esav was a man skillful in hunting, a man of the field; and Ya'aqov was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.

notes.official:
**The twin-character-contrast formula at v 27 is the foundational characterization of Esav and Ya'aqov.** Two parallel three-element formulae: Esav as *ish yodea tzayid ish sadeh* (*a man knowing hunting, a man of the field*); Ya'aqov as *ish tam yoshev ohalim* (*an *ish tam*, dwelling in tents*). The contrast is editorially-load-bearing — it justifies the parental-favoritism at v 28, establishes the narrative-grammar of all subsequent Esav-Ya'aqov interactions, and structurally aligns Esav with the Yishma'el / wilderness-pastoralist line and Ya'aqov with the Avraham-Yitzchaq / tent-dweller line.

**The *tam* lexeme — the chapter's translation crux.** *Tam* (תָּם) admits four principal readings, each lexically defensible. **R1 (ASV/KJV-revised/NRSV/NJPS dominant):** *quiet, mild, peaceable* — the family-character register; Ya'aqov the home-dwelling, mild-tempered, non-aggressive brother. **R2 (KJV original):** *plain, simple, straightforward* — the uncompounded-character register. **R3 (modern critical / NRSV-adjusted):** *blameless, complete, integral* — the moral-integrity register, aligning Ya'aqov's *tam* with Noah's *tamim* (Gen 6:9), Avraham's *tamim* (Gen 17:1, see the `tamim-walk-before-god-covenant` entry), and Job's *tam v-yashar* (Job 1:1, see the `tom-v-yashar` entry). **R4 (Fokkelman 1975 minority):** *innocent, naive* — ironic narrator-voice, Ya'aqov *appearing* uncomplicated while harboring the trickster-disposition.

The translation follows R1 (ASV-baseline *quiet*) as the dominant. **The full four-reading apparatus is treated in the `ish-tam-ish-sadeh-jacob-esau-contrast` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).** The key editorial point is that R3 — the moral-integrity reading — creates an **immediate narrative-tension** with the immediately-following narrative (vv 29-34: Ya'aqov manipulates the famished Esav; ch 27: Ya'aqov deceives the blind Yitzchaq). The tension is the editorial-point: Ya'aqov is named *tam* at v 27 and then narrated as *aqav* (supplanter) at vv 29-34 and ch 27. The integrity register is *in tension with* the supplant-acts; the tension is the Ya'aqov-character's signature. **Wenham** *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 177-178 develops this reading explicitly; **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 180-181 and **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 416-417 acknowledge both R1 and R3.

**The *ish sadeh* / *yoshev ohalim* contrast.** The dwelling-locale-pair structurally aligns Esav with the wilderness-pastoralist-hunter register (cf. the *pere adam* / Yishma'el characterization at Gen 16:12 and Gen 25:18; see the existing `pere-adam-wild-ass-prophecy` entry) and Ya'aqov with the patriarchal-tent-dweller register (Avraham at Gen 18:1, *yoshev petach ha-ohel*; the patriarchal *ohel* as the dwelling-locale of the covenantal line). The contrast is *not* nomad-vs.-settled-agriculturalist — both brothers are pastoralist; the difference is *where and how they dwell* within the pastoralist register. The locale-contrast subordinates Esav to the Yishma'el / collateral-line type and aligns Ya'aqov with the Avraham-Yitzchaq / covenantal-line type. The chapter is structurally preparing the covenant-line transmission to Ya'aqov.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 180-181; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 416-417; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 177-178; Fokkelman *Narrative Art in Genesis* 1975 pp. 86-87; Alter *Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 131.

paragraphs.text: וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב יִצְחָ֛ק אֶת־עֵשָׂ֖ו כִּי־צַ֣יִד בְּפִ֑יו וְרִבְקָ֖ה אֹהֶ֥בֶת אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: Now Yitzchaq loved Esav, because he ate of his venison; and Rivkah loved Ya'aqov.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֥זֶד יַעֲקֹ֖ב נָזִ֑יד וַיָּבֹ֥א עֵשָׂ֛ו מִן־הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה וְה֥וּא עָיֵֽף׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov boiled pottage. And Esav came in from the field, and he was faint.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַלְעִיטֵ֤נִי נָא֙ מִן־הָאָדֹ֤ם הָאָדֹם֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֥י עָיֵ֖ף אָנֹ֑כִי עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־שְׁמ֖וֹ אֱדֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And Esav said to Ya'aqov, Feed me, I pray you, with that same red pottage; for I am faint. Therefore was his name called Edom.

notes.official:
**The lentil-stew episode names the *adom* (red) connection that grounds Esav's secondary-name *Edom*.** *Hal'iteni-na min ha-adom ha-adom ha-zeh ki ayef anokhi al-ken qara shemo Edom* — *Feed me, I pray you, with that same red red stuff, for I am faint. Therefore was his name called Edom*. Three philological items of editorial significance:

**(a) The verb *hal'iteni* (הַלְעִיטֵנִי) is a HB hapax legomenon.** The root *l-ʿ-ṭ* does not recur in the canonical Hebrew Bible. The verb is attested in Talmudic Aramaic and Mishnaic Hebrew in the **force-feed register** — especially of cattle being force-fed (cf. *m. Shabbat 24:3*; *b. Shabbat 155b*). The lexeme's force-feed-register at Gen 25:30 stages Esav's exhaustion as a desperate-quantity request: *cram me with that red red stuff* — an inelegant verb-choice that the narrator deploys to characterize Esav's appetite-driven character. The hapax-status is editorially-deliberate. The ASV smoothing *feed me, I pray you* loses the force-feed register but preserves the petition-form.

**(b) The doubled *ha-adom ha-adom* is an emphatic-iterative redoubling.** The construction conveys (i) intensification of the red-color description; (ii) the staccato-speech of a famished man; (iii) the *adom* paronomasia twice at the cusp of the *Edom* naming-formula. **Alter** *Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 132 renders the doubling as *that red red stuff*; **Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 p. 196 as *some of that red, red stuff*. The WoH translation preserves ASV's smoother *that same red pottage* and surfaces the doubling in commentary.

**(c) The explicit Edom-etymology *al-ken qara shemo Edom*.** The closing-formula stages the second of the chapter's two Esav-naming-etymologies — paronomastic-foreshadowing at v 25 (*admoni*), explicit-naming-formula at v 30 (*Edom*). The two-stage etymology brackets the Esav-naming-arc. The Edom-etymology is **independent** of the Esav-etymology proper and stages Esav as the Edomite-progenitor figure for the wider Genesis arc (cf. Gen 36:8-9 *Esav hu Edom* — *Esav is Edom*).

The full philological apparatus and the Edom-historical-archaeological context (Knauf 1988, Bartlett 1989; the Edomite kingdom attested in the Neo-Assyrian record from the 9th century BCE forward; the archaeological sites at Buseirah, Tel el-Kheleifeh, Umm el-Biyara, Tawilan) are treated in the `esau-edom-name-etymology-double-play` glossary entry.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 181; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 417-418; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 p. 178; Alter *Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 132; Knauf 1988 *Midian*; Bartlett *Edom and the Edomites* 1989.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֑ב מִכְרָ֥ה כַיּ֛וֹם אֶת־בְּכֹֽרָתְךָ֖ לִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov said, Sell me first your birthright.

notes.official:
**Vv 31-34 stage the birthright-sale — the foundational HB episode for the *bekhorah* (firstborn-status) institution and the canonical-narrative source-text for the inter-brother birthright-transfer legal-form.** The *bekhorah* names the legal-juridical status of the firstborn son within the patriarchal-period inheritance-system: the double-portion of the paternal inheritance (formally codified at Deut 21:15-17), the patriarchal blessing (separately transferred at Gen 27), the headship-of-the-family-line, certain cultic-priestly responsibilities. The institution is *legally-transferable* between brothers under specified conditions, and the Gen 25 transaction is the canonical-HB instance of voluntary inter-brother birthright-transfer.

**The ANE legal-form: the Nuzi parallels, with critical caution.** The Nuzi tablets (Late-Bronze-Age Hurrian-Akkadian legal documents from northern Mesopotamia, 15th-14th centuries BCE) document multiple inter-brother inheritance-transfer transactions structurally parallel to the Gen 25 sale. The most-cited parallel is **HSS V 67** (the *Tupkitilla / Kurpazah* tablet): a brother sells his inheritance-share to another brother for three sheep. **Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 195-196 develops the Nuzi-parallel argument extensively and treats Gen 25 as documenting a real ANE legal-institution-form. **Critical caution**: **Selman** 1976 *Tyndale Bulletin* and **Van Seters** 1975 *Abraham in History and Tradition* (Yale) review the Speiser-era Nuzi-parallel arguments and find that some of the early-mid-20th-century parallels were *overdrawn*. **Greengus** 1975 *JAOS* 95 and **Eichler** 1989 *JANES* 18 conclude that the *basic legal-form* of brother-to-brother inheritance-transfer is well-attested across the ANE legal corpora, but the *specific Nuzi-Gen 25 parallels* are less precise than the early-Speiser arguments suggested. The modern critical consensus: the legal-form is plausible-ANE-attested but the specific Nuzi-Hurrian context is not required; the institutional setting is plausible Late-Bronze / Iron-I West-Semitic legal-practice. The full apparatus is treated in the `bekhorah-birthright-firstborn-status` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).

**The four-step legal-juridical sequence at vv 31-33.** **(i) Ya'aqov's request — the legal-immediacy formula.** *Mikhrah ka-yom et-bekhoratkha li* — *sell me today your birthright*. The phrase *ka-yom* is the legal-immediacy marker specifying immediate-effective transaction. **(ii) Esav's response — the legal-justification clause** (v 32). *Hineh anokhi holekh la-mut, v-lamah zeh li b'khorah* — *Behold, I am about to die; and what profit shall the birthright do me?*. The clause is a legal-justification for sale: Esav names a contingency (imminent death from hunger / from the wilderness-hunt) that renders the birthright valueless to him. The justification-clause is the legal-precondition for voluntary alienation-of-inheritance under standard ANE inheritance-law. **(iii) Ya'aqov's oath-demand — the legal-binding instrument** (v 33a). *Hishav'ah li ka-yom* — *swear to me today*. A sale-by-oath in the ANE legal-context is irrevocable. **(iv) Esav's oath and the legal-completion** (v 33b). *Va-yishava lo va-yimkor et-bekhorato l-Ya'aqov* — *and he swore to him, and he sold his birthright to Ya'aqov*. The legal-form is now complete.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 181-182; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 416-417; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 195-196; Selman 1976 *Tyndale Bulletin*; Van Seters 1975 *Abraham in History and Tradition*; Greengus 1975 *JAOS* 95; Eichler 1989 *JANES* 18.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר עֵשָׂ֔ו הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י הוֹלֵ֖ךְ לָמ֑וּת וְלָמָּה־זֶּ֥ה לִ֖י בְּכֹרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Esav said, Behold, I am about to die; and what profit shall the birthright do to me?

notes.official:
**Esav's response — the legal-justification clause.** *Hineh anokhi holekh la-mut, v-lamah zeh li b'khorah* — *Behold, I am about to die; and what profit shall the birthright do me?*. Two readings: **(i) the literal hyperbolic reading** — Esav exaggerates his hunger (he is exhausted from the field but not literally dying); the hyperbole names a *valuation-mismatch* between the immediate-need (food) and the long-term-asset (birthright). **(ii) the wilderness-pastoralist-mortality reading** — Esav's *ish sadeh* register exposes him to genuine mortality-risk from the hunt; the *holekh la-mut* names a real-and-ongoing condition rather than a hyperbolic moment. Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 182 reads the line as Esav's character-revealing self-rationalization: the rhetorical question *and what profit shall the birthright do me?* exposes Esav's preference for the immediate over the deferred. The clause functions as the **legal-justification for sale** under standard ANE inheritance-law: the seller must articulate a reason for voluntary alienation.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 182; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 416-417; Alter *Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 132.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֗ב הִשָּׁ֤בְעָה לִּי֙ כַּיּ֔וֹם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע ל֑וֹ וַיִּמְכֹּ֥ר אֶת־בְּכֹרָת֖וֹ לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov said, Swear to me first; and he swore to him; and he sold his birthright to Ya'aqov.

notes.official:
**The oath-demand and the legal-completion.** *Hishav'ah li ka-yom va-yishava lo va-yimkor et-bekhorato l-Ya'aqov* — *Swear to me today; and he swore to him, and he sold his birthright to Ya'aqov*. The oath-demand is the legal-binding instrument: a sale-by-oath in the ANE legal-context is irrevocable, the deity invoked as witness to the transaction. The verb *makhar* (qal imperfect with vav-consecutive) marks the legal-completion: the sale is now juridically-binding. The four-step sequence (request, justification, oath, completion) is now closed.

Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 182; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 416-417.

paragraphs.text: וְיַעֲקֹ֞ב נָתַ֣ן לְעֵשָׂ֗ו לֶ֚חֶם וּנְזִ֣יד עֲדָשִׁ֔ים וַיֹּ֣אכַל וַיֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ וַיִּ֥בֶז עֵשָׂ֖ו אֶת־הַבְּכֹרָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov gave Esav bread and pottage of lentils; and he ate and drank, and rose up, and went his way: so Esav despised his birthright.

notes.official:
**The narrator's editorial moral-verdict.** *V-Ya'aqov natan l-Esav lechem u-n-zid adashim va-yokhal va-yesht va-yaqam va-yelekh va-yivez Esav et-ha-bekhorah* — *and Ya'aqov gave Esav bread and pottage of lentils; and he ate, and drank, and rose up, and went his way: so Esav despised his birthright*. The four staccato verbs (*va-yokhal*, *va-yesht*, *va-yaqam*, *va-yelekh* — *and he ate, and drank, and rose, and went*) deliberately stage Esav's animal-immediacy-of-appetite; **Alter** *Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 132 notes the rhetorical effect. The closing verb *va-yivez* (qal impf 3ms of *bazah* — *despise, scorn, hold in contempt*) carries the narrator's **editorial moral-verdict** and is treated extensively in the `va-yivez-esav-et-ha-bekhorah-despising-birthright` glossary entry (new at v2.23.0).

**The *bazah* lexeme** is the HB's primary verb for *despise, hold in contempt, treat as worthless*. Cross-corpus: Num 15:31 (the apostate who despises the word of YHWH); 1 Sam 17:42 (Goliath despising the youth David); 2 Sam 6:16 (Michal despising David's dance); 2 Kgs 19:21 / Isa 37:22 (the virgin daughter of Zion despising Sennacherib); Mal 1:6-7 (the priests despising the name of YHWH); Isa 53:3 (the suffering servant *nivzeh* — despised). The verb's consistent register is strong-negative valuation. Its application to Esav at v 34 is the narrator's severe-verdict.

**NT reception at Hebrews 12:16-17.** *Mē tis pornos ē bebēlos hōs Ēsau, hos anti brōseōs mias apedeto ta prōtotokia heautou* — *Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person (bebēlos), as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his own birthright*. The Greek *bebēlos* (*profane, unhallowed, irreligious*) renders the *va-yivez* verdict into early-Christian theological vocabulary as *profanity / unholiness*. Esav becomes the type-figure of the profane-firstborn. The reception extends across the patristic and medieval Christian tradition: **Origen** *Homilies on Genesis* XII; **Augustine** *De Civitate Dei* XV-XVI (Esav as type of the earthly-city); **Calvin** *Institutes* III (Esav as evidence of reprobation). The Lectionary tradition pairs Gen 25:31-34 with Heb 12:16-17 across the Christian liturgical-year. **The reception is flagged-not-preempted.**

**Rabbinic reception at Genesis Rabbah 63:11.** The rabbinic tradition expands the *va-yivez* verdict into **five sins** committed by Esav on the day of the birthright-sale: (i) violation of a betrothed maiden; (ii) murder; (iii) denial of the resurrection of the dead; (iv) denial of divine providence; (v) despising the birthright. The midrashic-expansion amplifies the v 34 text into a comprehensive characterological condemnation. Rashi at Gen 25:34 cites Genesis Rabbah 63:11 and the comprehensive-contempt reading. **The reception is flagged-not-preempted.**

**Modern critical reading.** Modern critical scholarship (Sarna, Westermann, Wenham, Hamilton, Alter, Speiser) reads the *va-yivez* verdict more narrowly: the verse is the narrator's verdict on the *immediacy-of-appetite-over-long-term-promise* pattern. Esav values immediate satisfaction over deferred patriarchal blessing — the contempt-verdict targets this specific decision-making pattern, not a comprehensive moral failure.
